page: Amazon Web Services r7i.large is a memory-optimized instance designed for workloads requiring a high memory-to-CPU ratio. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs from 1 physical core on a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Hardware instruction capabilities include AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and AES-NI cryptography. Memory provisioning includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation. The server includes no bundled local storage and supplies a 1 Gbps baseline network interface without included complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark profiles demonstrate steady single-thread performance alongside bounded multi-threaded processing. In single-core testing, the instance achieved average results across Geekbench (1691.0) and stress-ng (1909.48), with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 29.32 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks reflect the two-vCPU ceiling, registering lower relative percentiles with a PassMark CPU score of 3413.47 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2066.0. Memory bandwidth reached 151.29 GB/sec on cached small blocks, decreasing to 10.99 GB/sec read and 11.68 GB/sec write on larger uncached transfers. Redis throughput reached 2.69 million operations per second, while static web throughput measured 4.58 GB/sec.

The architectural profile prioritizes DDR5 memory capacity per core over dense parallel computation. With 16 GB assigned across two logical execution threads, workloads benefit from high memory density without the overhead of unused CPU cores. The primary operational tradeoffs involve the complete absence of integrated local NVMe storage and modest network bandwidth, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data. The r7i.large is appropriate for memory-sensitive deployments such as small Redis or Memcached instances, intermediate database nodes, queue processors, and microservices requiring substantial memory footprints but modest compute throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, the configuration supplies 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with dedicated scheduling, supported by 16.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 5 GHz. Instruction support includes Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. The instance provisions no local storage and relies on network-attached storage alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate balanced single-core throughput, recording average scores in single-core stress-ng and Geekbench execution, while multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth fall into lower brackets due to the two-vCPU physical limit. With its high memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, the r7i.large is suited for moderately sized in-memory caches, lightweight database servers, microservices with high working-set memory requirements, and memory-bound background tasks.
